title.zh: 授权印制和发行半邮政邮票为 Jose Rizal 百年庆典筹集资金并拨付必要经费的法案
title.en: An Act Authorizing the Printing and Issue of Semi-Postal Stamps to Raise Funds to be Used for the Jose Rizal Centennial Celebration and Appropriating the Necessary Funds Therefor
title.orig: An Act Authorizing the Printing and Issue of Semi-Postal Stamps to Raise Funds to be Used for the Jose Rizal Centennial Celebration and Appropriating the Necessary Funds Therefor

source.name: LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation）

completenessNote: 全文，共 5 条；逐字取自 LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation） 官方页面（statutes/repacts/ra1961/ra_3021_1961.html），未改写、未摘译、未节选；原文语言：英语。 条文抬头依源文为 “Section N.” 等形式，本库统一规范为 “Section N.”；首行抬头与条内标题的分段依源文块级边界还原。

text.en: To raise funds for the celebration of the centenary of the birth of Dr. Jose Rizal, the Postmaster General, subject to the approval of the Department Head, is hereby authorized to order the printing and issue of semi-postal stamps for a period of three years from the date of the approval of this Act, to be known as Rizal Centennial issue, of one or more denominations, with face value showing the regular postage charge and the additional amount to be fixed by said Postmaster General with the recommendation of the Jose Rizal National Centennial Commission.
These postage stamps shall bear an appropriate vignette to further perpetuate the memory of the national hero.

The additional sum realized from sale of these postage stamps shall be deposited with the Bureau of the Treasury and shall be placed at the disposal of the Jose Rizal National Centennial Commission, created by Executive Order Numbered Fifty-two on August ten, nineteen hundred and fifty-four, subject to the usual accounting and auditing regulations.

There is hereby appropriated, out of any funds in the National Treasury not otherwise appropriated, the sum of thirty thousand pesos to defray the expenses for the preparation of the designs of the stamps, transportation, insurance and other expenses.

This Act shall take effect upon its approval.
Approved: February 28, 1961.
